Subject: Fleet deployment — license vs support split and escalation path

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for yesterday’s demo. We’re getting the internal procurement and IT finance teams aligned and have two questions that are blocking our CapEx approval: 1) how you recommend we split the “platform fee” between a capitalized license and an operational support line item for our auditors, and 2) what the formal escalation path / SLA credit mechanics look like for Private (VPC) deployments.

Context: HealthTech is planning an initial fleet with 12 dedicated nodes (multi-region) and a 3‑year commitment. The CFO needs a clear allocation on the order form (license vs support) and a one‑pager describing the SLA credit ladder for outages and data-plane incidents.

Can you send a simple cost partitioning example (annualized/macro numbers will do) and the contact/escalation list we should put into our procurement package? I attached our standard procurement form so you can see the format.

Appreciate it — Olivia

Folks — looping you in on HealthTech’s ask (see below). High priority from a procurement perspective; CFO wants the split for CapEx/OpEx classification and they also want a clear SLA/escalation one‑pager.

Quick proposed options to discuss:
- Option A: Explicit split — show platform fee as 60% perpetual license (capitalizable) + 40% 36‑month support/services (OpEx).
- Option B: Prepaid platform fee amortized monthly over 36 months with a separate smaller annual support line (simpler for procurement but may not satisfy auditors).
- Option C: Node‑based license (fixed units) + metered runtime (tokens) under support — good for our cost transparency asks.

Rishi — can you run a quick cost model for all three and attach an example workbook?
Sean — we need to confirm acceptable accounting language for the amortization approach and whether we can offer a migration credit in year 1 without affecting the customer’s CapEx booking.

I’ll draft the SLA one‑pager and escalation points; if Legal has to see contract language, include Michael (HealthTech legal) when they send redlines.

—Chloe

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 11:05 AM chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Folks — looping you in on HealthTech’s ask (see below). High priority from a procurement perspective; CFO wants the split for CapEx/OpEx classification and they also want a clear SLA/escalation one‑pager.

Thanks — I ran a quick model and attached a workbook (cost_model_v2.xlsx). High‑level takeaways:

- Recommended commercial framing: 60/40 split (license/support) for the 3‑year commit. That treats 60% of the one‑time platform fee as capitalizable (license) and 40% as an annual support/service band amortized over the same term.
- Migration credit: propose a 10% first‑year credit applied to the platform fee (not support) — this preserves the customer’s ability to book CapEx while we absorb onboarding effort.
- SLA credits: formalize a three‑tier ladder (P1 > 4 hrs availability drop => 5% credit; P1 > 8 hrs => 15% credit; P1 full region outage 24+ hrs => 40% credit). Credits applied against support line only.
- Exit/cancellation: recommend a pro‑rated refund on license portion with a 60‑day wind‑down to avoid revenue recognition disputes.

I included a tab showing monthly amortization schedule so the CFO can see Opex vs CapEx line items.

attachment: cost_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

—Rishi

Good options — a couple of practical negotiation notes:

1) For enterprise deals like this, the CFO usually accepts the amortized prepaid approach if we supply GL mapping language they can push to auditors. I can draft that bullet.
2) To keep procurement moving, offer a limited migration credit (10%) + first‑quarter free on‑call retainer (we absorb 3 shifts) in lieu of a larger percent discount. That keeps headline ARR up while giving them operational comfort.
3) SLA ladder is fine but add a clause for Agreed Recovery Plan (ARP) — once invoked it triggers a named oncall escalation to our SRE lead (we should include contact name and mobile).
4) Legal will ask about indemnities and data handling for VPCs — anticipate 2–3 redline requests.

Sean — can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with a 36‑month amortization on our order form? If not, we’ll pivot to a license + support line item as separate invoices.

I’ve cc’d Olivia so she can flag which of these she needs in writing for procurement.

—Marissa

Chloe / team —

Thanks for the clear options. I’ve attached our redlines to the master terms for your review (HT-DR_contract_redlines.pdf). A few items to flag from Legal:

- We need to see specific language that describes what is capitalizable (license) vs what is a service; auditors here are strict.
- SLA credits: please confirm whether credits can reduce the support invoices only and cannot be used to offset license amortization (that is a firm ask).
- Escalation: we need named contacts and an SLA response time for second‑line SRE (phone and email).

I appreciate Rishi’s ladder — minor tweaks requested in the doc. If you can provide a short addendum that maps platform fee line items to accounting codes, that will help accelerate our procurement approval.

Olivia / Michael — thanks for the clear feedback and the redlines. Next steps consolidated here so procurement has a single action list: 

1) Commercial proposal: we’ll send a formal order form with Option A (60/40 license/support) and a parallel amortized invoice view for your CFO to show monthly Opex. Rishi attached the workbook for preview.
2) Credits & onboarding: we’ll include a 10% migration credit applied only to the license portion (preserves CapEx). Also offering three shifts of on‑call retainer in Q1 as an operational concession.
3) SLA & escalation: we’ll produce one‑pager describing the SLA ladder, named SRE escalation contacts (mobile + email), and the Agreed Recovery Plan trigger. Credits will apply to support invoices only per request.
4) Legal redlines: we’ll review HT‑DR_contract_redlines.pdf and prepare a short addendum that maps platform fee accounting to suggested GL codes. Please expect that within 48 hours.
